criteria.criterion: A function in tools/release takes the directory as a parameter, lists files with `git -C <top directory> ls-files -z --cached --others --exclude-standard` and checks each path with `module.CheckFilePath` from golang.org/x/mod; it fails with one line `<path>: <the error CheckFilePath returns>` per rejected path, in the order git lists them. A check that skips untracked files, or a hand-written character rule in place of CheckFilePath, is a violation.
criteria.evidence: paths.go rejectedPaths: rev-parse top, git -C top ls-files -z --cached --others --exclude-standard, module.CheckFilePath, lines p+': '+err

criteria.criterion: `release paths` prints those lines on stdout, then `release: the module zip rejects <n> path(s)` on stderr, exit 1; with none it prints nothing, exit 0; given any argument it prints `usage: release paths` on stderr, exit 2; when git fails it prints `release: <git's error on one line>` on stderr, exit 1. Paths are the top directory's even when started in a subdirectory.
criteria.evidence: paths.go paths() implements each branch; top via rev-parse --show-toplevel. Exit codes are not unit-tested, but the code is direct.

criteria.criterion: The usage line of tools/release is exactly `usage: release notes <from> <to> | paths | prepare <version> [--dry-run] | publish <version> [--wait <duration>] [--dry-run]`, and the command's doc comment lists paths.
criteria.evidence: main.go usage string and doc comment line for paths

criteria.criterion: `TestPaths` in tools/release holds the four cases of the brief, each a fixture repository in a temporary directory addressed with git -C: a committed `it's repo/.keep` gives its line; an untracked, not ignored `a'b.txt` gives its line; the same a'b.txt listed in .gitignore gives no line; a fixture with only go.mod and x.go gives no line. No ' path is written into the repository's tree, and no test touches the network.
criteria.evidence: paths_test.go TestPaths four subtests with newRepo temp fixtures, asserting exact lines

criteria.criterion: `TestRepositoryPaths` in tools/release runs the function on this repository and fails with the same lines; it skips, saying why, when `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` fails or the top directory's go.mod does not declare `module github.com/mvelosop/vloop`. It passes on this repository under the go check.
criteria.evidence: paths_test.go TestRepositoryPaths with both skips; go.log shows tools/release ok

criteria.criterion: golang.org/x/mod is a direct requirement of the module at v0.37.0 and go.sum is what `go mod tidy` writes for it (the go check's `go mod tidy -diff` prints nothing).
criteria.evidence: go.mod direct require v0.37.0 without // indirect; go.sum h1 and go.mod lines; go check exit 0

criteria.criterion: tools/release/README.md has a `## paths` section saying what paths prints and when it exits 1. Nothing under .vloop/ is edited.
criteria.evidence: README.md ## paths section; the only .vloop changes are driver records

notes: Exit-code paths of release paths (usage, git failure) have no test; the brief did not require one.
